title: Academic Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for academic vocabulary.

items.definition_en: a system of ideas used to organise a subject
items.example: The paper proposes a framework for analysis.

items.definition_en: a belief accepted without proof
items.example: The model rests on a questionable assumption.

items.definition_en: to explain the meaning of information
items.example: Researchers interpreted the findings cautiously.

items.definition_en: supported by facts or logical reasoning
items.example: The criticism remains valid today.

title: Environment Advanced
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for environment advanced.

items.definition_en: the variety of living species in an area
items.example: Intensive farming can reduce biodiversity.

items.definition_en: damage that reduces quality or value
items.example: Soil degradation threatens food production.

items.definition_en: able to continue without exhausting resources
items.example: The city needs a sustainable transport system.

items.definition_en: gas or substance released into the air
items.example: The law sets limits on carbon emissions.

title: Education Advanced
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for education advanced.

items.definition_en: the theory and practice of teaching
items.example: Digital tools can support effective pedagogy.

items.definition_en: the level achieved in education
items.example: Family income can affect academic attainment.

items.definition_en: the ability to read and write
items.example: The initiative promotes adult literacy.

items.definition_en: related to skills for a particular job
items.example: Vocational training may improve employment prospects.

title: Technology
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for technology.

items.definition_en: use of machines to perform work automatically
items.example: Automation has transformed manufacturing.

items.definition_en: a set of rules for solving a problem
items.example: The platform uses an algorithm to rank results.

items.definition_en: freedom from unwanted access to personal information
items.example: Users are concerned about data privacy.

items.definition_en: inequality in access to digital technology
items.example: Rural investment could narrow the digital divide.

title: Economics
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for economics.

items.definition_en: a general rise in prices
items.example: High inflation reduces household purchasing power.

items.definition_en: income received by an organisation
items.example: Tax revenue funds public services.

items.definition_en: money given to support an activity
items.example: The government introduced a renewable-energy subsidy.

items.definition_en: the use of goods, services, or resources
items.example: Energy consumption fell during the summer.

title: Government and Public Policy
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for government and public policy.

items.definition_en: an official rule controlling an activity
items.example: New regulation protects consumers.

items.definition_en: to put a plan or policy into effect
items.example: The council will implement the policy next year.

items.definition_en: responsibility for decisions and results
items.example: Transparent reporting improves public accountability.

items.definition_en: laws considered collectively
items.example: The legislation sets stricter safety standards.

title: Globalisation
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for globalisation.

items.definition_en: mutual dependence between people or countries
items.example: Trade creates economic interdependence.

items.definition_en: operating in several countries
items.example: A multinational company opened a local office.

items.definition_en: using an external company to perform work
items.example: Outsourcing reduced operating costs.

items.definition_en: taking place between different countries
items.example: Online services enable cross-border trade.

title: Health Systems
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for health systems.

items.definition_en: the delivery of health services
items.example: Rural healthcare provision remains uneven.

items.definition_en: identification of an illness
items.example: Early diagnosis improves survival rates.

items.definition_en: medical action intended to prevent illness
items.example: Preventive care can lower long-term costs.

items.definition_en: the quality of being easy to reach or use
items.example: Clinics improved the accessibility of treatment.

title: Urbanisation
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for urbanisation.

items.definition_en: uncontrolled expansion of a city
items.example: Urban sprawl increases dependence on cars.

items.definition_en: the number of people living in an area
items.example: Population density is highest near the centre.

items.definition_en: related to a city government
items.example: Municipal authorities manage waste collection.

items.definition_en: building an area again in a new way
items.example: The waterfront redevelopment created public space.

title: Social Issues
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for social issues.

items.definition_en: being prevented from participating in society
items.example: Unemployment may lead to social exclusion.

items.definition_en: unfair treatment based on personal characteristics
items.example: The law prohibits workplace discrimination.

items.definition_en: at risk of harm or disadvantage
items.example: The programme supports vulnerable families.

items.definition_en: support intended to protect people's well-being
items.example: Welfare payments provide temporary assistance.

title: Scientific Research
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for scientific research.

items.definition_en: a proposed explanation that can be tested
items.example: The results support the original hypothesis.

items.definition_en: a factor that can change in an experiment
items.example: Researchers controlled every relevant variable.

items.definition_en: to repeat a study and obtain comparable results
items.example: Another laboratory failed to replicate the finding.

items.definition_en: based on observation or experiment
items.example: The claim lacks empirical evidence.

title: Employment
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for employment.

items.definition_en: all people available for work
items.example: Older workers form a growing share of the workforce.

items.definition_en: the likelihood that employment will continue
items.example: Temporary contracts offer little job security.

items.definition_en: the process of finding new employees
items.example: Online recruitment has widened the applicant pool.

items.definition_en: payment received for work
items.example: The role offers fair remuneration.

title: Crime and Justice
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for crime and justice.

items.definition_en: something that discourages an action
items.example: Visible policing can act as a deterrent.

items.definition_en: helping an offender return to normal life
items.example: Education is central to prisoner rehabilitation.

items.definition_en: legal action against an accused person
items.example: The evidence was insufficient for prosecution.

items.definition_en: related to young people who are not adults
items.example: The city introduced a juvenile crime programme.

title: Culture and Identity
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for culture and identity.

items.definition_en: adoption of another group's culture
items.example: Rapid assimilation may weaken minority languages.

items.definition_en: a shared expectation within a culture
items.example: Ideas about punctuality are a cultural norm.

items.definition_en: the feeling of being accepted by a group
items.example: Community events create a sense of belonging.

items.definition_en: including several cultures
items.example: The school serves a multicultural neighbourhood.

title: Academic Collocations
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for academic collocations.

items.definition_en: to identify an important difference
items.example: The article draws a distinction between need and demand.

items.definition_en: to create a difficult problem
items.example: Rapid growth poses a challenge for planners.

items.definition_en: a basic cause hidden beneath visible effects
items.example: The policy does not address the underlying cause.

items.definition_en: a line of reasoning that strongly persuades
items.example: The author presents a compelling argument for reform.

title: Lexical Precision
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for lexical precision.

items.definition_en: to become or make something smaller
items.example: Public confidence diminished after the scandal.

items.definition_en: large in amount or importance
items.example: The project requires substantial investment.

items.definition_en: too small to be important
items.example: The change had a negligible effect.

items.definition_en: to assign resources for a purpose
items.example: The council allocated funds to housing.

title: Paraphrasing Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for paraphrasing vocabulary.

items.definition_en: to form or be considered as something
items.example: Small firms constitute most local businesses.

items.definition_en: to show something clearly with evidence
items.example: The figures demonstrate a consistent trend.

items.definition_en: mainly or mostly
items.example: The region is predominantly rural.

items.definition_en: a result of an action or condition
items.example: Higher costs were an unintended consequence.
